entries.title: Bravox Credit
entries.keywords: bravox bravoxcredit credit card cards approval odds product startup side project engine pre approval estimator
entries.short: Bravox is a credit card pre-approval estimator Abhi built and shipped solo, live at bravoxcredit.com.
entries.body: Bravox is a full-stack credit card pre-approval estimator Abhi built and shipped solo, live at bravoxcredit.com. It evaluates 27 cards across 3 credit bureaus, judging each card against the bureau its issuer typically pulls. He built it because most credit tools exist to sell you cards, not tell you the truth, and he wanted the honest one.

entries.title: How Bravox estimates odds
entries.keywords: how works estimate calculate compute approval odds probability algorithm model scoring score formula engine tier tiers weights weighting margin method logic
entries.short: Score tiers decide eligibility; a weighted margin over score, utilization, and inquiries sets the odds.
entries.body: The engine works in two steps. Score tiers gate eligibility: each card has a minimum tier plus ceilings for utilization and recent inquiries. Then a weighted margin sets the odds: 50% how far the score clears the card's tier floor (full credit at 60 points above it), 30% utilization headroom, and 20% inquiry headroom, mapped onto a 45 to 96% band. Every result comes with plain-language reasons, including why a card is out of reach.

entries.title: Why the odds never reach 100%
entries.keywords: 96 100 percent ceiling cap maximum max guarantee guaranteed certain certainty sure floor 45 band range limit
entries.short: Bravox caps odds at 96% because issuers weigh factors the engine can't see.
entries.body: Bravox caps odds at 96% on purpose. Issuers also weigh income, debt-to-income, account age, and internal risk models the engine can't see, so promising near-certainty would be dishonest. The 45% floor exists because clearing every threshold still isn't a coin flip.

entries.title: Per-bureau logic
entries.keywords: bureau bureaus experian equifax transunion pull pulls inquiry issuer issuers chase amex american express capital one citi discover wells fargo bank america opensky
entries.short: Bravox judges each card against the bureau its issuer typically pulls.
entries.body: Issuers usually check one credit bureau, and scores can differ between bureaus. Bravox tags each issuer with the bureau it typically pulls, based on community reports, and evaluates its cards against that score: American Express, Chase, Citi, Discover, Wells Fargo, and Bank of America map to Experian, Capital One checks all three, and OpenSky runs no credit check. Users can enter a score per bureau; Bravox doesn't invent separate cutoffs for each one.

entries.title: Approval odds versus fit
entries.keywords: fit recommendation recommend recommended best card ranking rank ranked secured starter mismatch right card
entries.short: Bravox scores fit separately from approval, so near-certain but poor matches sink.
entries.body: Approval odds and fit are different questions. Someone with an 810 score will almost certainly get a secured starter card, but it's a poor recommendation. So Bravox scores fit separately: each tier a card sits below the user's profile costs 12% of its score, floored at 30%, which lifts better-matched cards to the top.

entries.title: Chase 5/24
entries.keywords: fivetwentyfour chase rule new accounts opened 24 months
entries.short: Bravox models Chase's community-reported 5/24 rule.
entries.body: Bravox models Chase's community-reported 5/24 rule: with five or more new personal cards in the last 24 months, most Chase cards are marked out of reach, and the result says why. A free 5/24 counter on the site shows when the oldest account drops off.

entries.title: Bravox architecture
entries.keywords: architecture backend frontend fastapi nextjs typescript react postgres postgresql neon render vercel database api deploy deployed hosting infrastructure
entries.short: Bravox runs Next.js on Vercel, FastAPI on Render, and PostgreSQL on Neon.
entries.body: Bravox runs a Next.js and TypeScript frontend on Vercel, a FastAPI backend on Render, and a PostgreSQL database on Neon for users, sessions, saved checks, feedback, and the waitlist. The frontend talks to the API through a typed client, and the odds engine is plain Python with no framework dependencies, so its rules stay testable on their own.

entries.title: Security and privacy in Bravox
entries.keywords: security secure privacy safe safety password passwords hashing hash pbkdf2 rate limiting lockout csp hsts headers ssn hard pull bank login audit auth
entries.short: Bravox asks for no SSN, runs no hard pull, and needs no bank login.
entries.body: Bravox asks for no SSN, runs no hard pull, and needs no bank login. It was deployed solo to production with secure auth (PBKDF2 password hashing and login lockout), rate limiting, CSP and HSTS headers, and request-size limits, and consumer identifiers in its audit and feedback logs are hashed, never stored raw.

entries.short: Keystroke is an iOS app that turns user images into custom Apple Wallet passes.
entries.body: Keystroke is an iOS app Abhi built with SwiftUI and a FastAPI backend that turns a user's images into custom Apple Wallet passes. The backend processes the image uploads and handles Apple Wallet's pass-signing requirements.

entries.title: How Keystroke signs passes
entries.keywords: signing sign signature signed certificate manifest sha1 hash bundle pass json pkcs backend server
entries.short: Wallet passes must be signed, and Keystroke's FastAPI backend handles that.
entries.body: Apple Wallet only accepts signed passes. A pass is a bundle of files, such as pass.json and its images, plus a manifest that lists a SHA-1 hash of every file and a signature over that manifest made with an Apple-issued certificate. Keystroke's FastAPI backend handles those signing requirements after processing the uploaded image.

entries.title: How this assistant works
entries.keywords: assistant agent bot chatbot engine coded built works retrieval bm25 model
entries.short: I'm a retrieval engine that runs in your browser and answers only from Abhi's published record.
entries.body: I'm a retrieval engine with two small trained models, running in your browser, not a chatbot model. Each question is spell-checked against the record and routed by rules first: greetings, private topics, internal Quest details, and off-topic requests. Everything else is ranked by BM25 keyword search blended with an intent classifier and semantic embeddings, both trained on this record. If the best match clears an honesty floor, I answer from those entries only and cite them; if not, I say it isn't in the record. The Sandbox section shows every stage, the model card, and a live semantic map.

entries.body: He doesn't rank his projects publicly, but they differ in scope. Bravox is the largest: a full-stack product he took from zero to production solo, live at bravoxcredit.com. Keystroke takes him onto iOS, with a FastAPI backend that handles Apple Wallet's signing requirements. The sleep dashboard and the YouTube algorithm are his applied ML work.

entries.title: FICO and VantageScore
entries.keywords: fico vantagescore vantage scoring models credit score
entries.short: Bravox uses the score model users report and never converts between FICO and VantageScore.
entries.body: Users tell Bravox which model their score comes from and can add the other. Odds use FICO-style tiers and the FICO score whenever one is given; both scores are shown side by side, and Bravox never converts one into the other.
